html:
The Kwantlen are a Stó:lō people of the lower Fraser River, in British Columbia. They speak Halkomelem, a Coast Salish language. Before Europeans came they were one of the strongest peoples on the river, with their main village near today's New Westminster.

In 1827 the Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Langley upriver, and many Kwantlen moved to be near it, to trade salmon and furs. Their main home is still McMillan Island, across from the fort. In 1858 the fort was where the colony of British Columbia was proclaimed. A university in the Fraser Valley takes its name from them. Neighbours: Katzie and Kwikwetlem.
